transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I feel like how I look and what I weigh is the only thing that matters about me now, and it’s starting to take over my life around food. It’s just constantly on my mind, and I don't really know how to make it stop.
To help me understand better, do you find yourself severely restricting how much you eat, or do you have times where you feel you lose control and eat a very large amount of food?

I actually do both. I try to restrict myself by skipping meals or eating only plain chicken and veggies because I'm terrified of gaining weight, but then I'll have these nights where a switch flips and I lose complete control. I'll end up shoveling down huge amounts of bread, leftovers, and chips in under an hour until I'm uncomfortably full and just can't stop.
After these episodes of losing control and eating, do you do anything to try to prevent weight gain, such as making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?

It's really hard to admit, but I usually end up forcing myself to throw up afterward to 'undo the damage' so I don't wake up heavier. I'll also resort to skipping meals the next day to try and make up for what I ate.
To help me better understand your physical health, could you please share your current height and weight, or if you've recently been told you are underweight?
I don't know my exact height and weight right now. But lately, friends and family have been commenting on how "lean" I've been looking.
Have you experienced significant weight loss recently, or has a doctor ever told you that your weight is dangerously low for your height?

No, a doctor has never told me that my weight is dangerously low. People have just commented on me looking "lean" since my separation, but I track my weight meticulously because I'm terrified of gaining even a single pound.
How often do these episodes of losing control and throwing up occur, and for how many months has this been happening?

This cycle of overeating and then throwing up or skipping meals has been happening at least a couple of times every week, sometimes more if I'm really stressed. It's been going on for about five months now, starting shortly after I moved out following my separation.
Since you mentioned you track your weight meticulously, could you share your current weight and height, or at least a close estimate of them?
I'm not actually sure of my exact height. To be honest, I prefer not to share the exact numbers on the scale because focusing on the specific weight makes me really anxious.
Even without sharing the exact numbers, would you say your current weight is significantly below what is considered normal for your height, or is it generally within a normal range?

I'm not entirely sure about the official medical ranges, but I think I'm probably within a normal range. I just constantly worry about gaining weight and feeling soft, so even being at a normal weight makes me feel incredibly anxious.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms recently, such as feeling constantly cold, dizzy, unusually fatigued, or, if you menstruate, has your period stopped or become irregular?

Well, as a man, the question about periods doesn't apply to me, and I haven't really noticed feeling constantly cold or dizzy. However, I do feel incredibly drained and exhausted the day after a bad night of binging and throwing up. It makes it really hard to focus properly on my work at the rescue center.
To help me understand your physical status better without focusing on the exact scale number, approximately how much weight have you lost since your separation five months ago?

I honestly don't know the exact amount of weight I've lost since the separation. I just obsessively track my weight every single day to make sure it doesn't go up at all, though family and friends have definitely noticed that I look a lot leaner now.
Since you track your weight daily, would you be comfortable sharing if your current weight is below what is typical for your height, or have you had to buy much smaller clothing sizes recently?

I don't think I'm actually underweight for my height, and I haven't really had to buy significantly smaller clothes or anything. It's just that people around me have definitely noticed and commented on me looking a lot leaner lately.
Since sharing exact numbers is difficult, would you be comfortable sharing just your height and a general range of where your weight usually sits?

I'd really rather not focus on those numbers or even a range right now, if that's okay. Just trying to put a number on it makes me feel incredibly anxious and stressed. I really want to focus on how to stop this cycle instead.
